coverage_note: The readable opening solves the whole first part: the statement p -> (q -> (p and q)) is shown to be a tautology by the by-case method on p, and the simplification method is started. The rest of the video was past the cut.
concepts: The by-case method is called the most efficient method for tautology questions.
Worked example: with p = true, p -> (q -> (p and q)) becomes q -> q, which is true; with p = false the whole implication is true because false implies anything.
Both cases give true, and the two cases cover every interpretation, so the statement is a tautology.
Two useful shortcuts used in the solution: true -> A is A, and A -> A is always true.
The simplification route rewrites alpha -> beta as not alpha or beta.
